name: rescue_effect
description: Brown & Kodric-Brown (1977) rescue-effect archipelago: identical islands (same area and isolation) differing only in how strongly incoming propagules rescue present species from extinction. Coupling the immigration and extinction curves raises equilibrium richness and damps turnover; rescue_strength=0 reduces to the independent-curves MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium.

n_islands.description: Number of islands (rescue-strength levels, or replicates)

colonization_base.description: Per-species colonization prob at distance 0 (also the rescue probability)

extinction_base.description: Per-species baseline extinction prob at the reference area

rescue_min.description: Rescue strength on the first island (0 = no rescue = baseline M-W)

rescue_max.description: Rescue strength on the last island (linear across islands)

seed.description: RNG seed; each island uses seed + its index

island_00.doc:
One island under the MacArthur-Wilson model *with* the rescue effect.

Identical to :class:`MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess` (presence/absence of
``n_pool`` pool species on a single island; absent species colonize at
``c = colonization_base/(1+distance)``; present species go extinct at the
area-dependent base ``e``) **except** that the incoming colonization pressure
also rescues present populations: each tick a present species is rescued with
probability ``c`` and, if rescued, its extinction probability is reduced to
``e*(1 - rescue_strength)``.

Outputs mirror :class:`MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess` exactly (all
deltas, so the stores accumulate — the mass/length delta precedent), which
lets the study reuse :func:`viva_island_biogeography.viz.turnover_timeseries`
and :func:`viva_island_biogeography.viz.mw_rate_crossing` unchanged.

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
